references.title: DWDS: erinnern
references.supports: The Wortzerlegung is only er-; ⟨sich an etw., jmdn. erinnern⟩ is sense 1a; Etymologie (Pfeifer): a Präfixbildung (frühnhd. erinnern) belonging, like the simplex mhd. innern, to ahd. innaro 'inner'

references.title: DWDS: innern
references.supports: No headword innern: DWDS offers the adjective inner instead

references.title: en.wiktionary: erinnern
references.supports: From Middle High German erinnern, from er- + innern, from Old High German innarōn, from innar 'inner'

notes.rationale: The Canonical Form is the bare word erinnern, since the reflexive of the 🪞🧠💭 'remember' Reading lives in its frame, never in the Lemma (ADR 0052), so the Breakdown spells erinnern (ADR 0050). erinnern is a bottom word, as vergessen (ver · gess · en) is: its base innern is Middle High German and has no modern headword, so it has no word inside and no Constituents (user, #1241, 2026-10-25). DWDS splits off only er-, which is on the closed affix list, so the remainder inner is the Root, and the citation ending n is a Surface of the Ending -en, as in läch · el · n (ADR 0051).
